transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! It's great to speak with you. I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery that I can help with?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thank you for asking! I'm feeling pretty good overall, but I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as watering plants or doing some gentle pruning, about 1 week after your surgery. However, it's best to avoid anything that might get water in your eyes, and also avoid heavy lifting or bending. You can also consider wearing protective eyewear while gardening to be extra cautious.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, that makes sense. Thanks for the advice. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use the eye drops as was prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma, or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that! I have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light lately. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild, just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside might help. But if it's severe or you're experiencing significant pain, it's best to get in touch with your care team to have it checked.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that's reassuring to hear. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for answering all my questions, Dora. I really appreciate it. I don't have any more questions for now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions and put your mind at ease. Now, I just want to check: do you feel like all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you’ve answered everything I was wondering about. Thank you so much for your help!
